courses.title: Mathematical toolkit
courses.subtitle: Tools that make the ideas precise
prerequisites: Foundations; basic algebra and equation rearrangement. Toolkit practice is needed before advanced physics, not just the overview lessons.

courses.title: Classical mechanics
courses.subtitle: A bounded introductory course in motion and interactions
prerequisites: Foundations for introductory motion concepts; Mathematical toolkit for the extended calculus, vector and rotation sequence. Each lesson links its local prerequisites.

courses.title: Electricity & magnetism
courses.subtitle: Charges, fields and circuits
prerequisites: Foundations, Classical mechanics and Mathematical toolkit. Local links identify vectors, calculus, complex numbers and differential equations before they are used.
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory course, not advanced field theory, a complete university laboratory sequence, electrical-safety training or proof of mastery.

courses.title: Vibrations & waves
courses.subtitle: From repeated motion to interference
prerequisites: Mechanics and Mathematical toolkit, including trigonometry, derivatives, integrals, ODEs, complex numbers and eigenvectors; E&M for electromagnetic sections. Each lesson links its local prerequisites.
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory wave-model course, not a full university waves/optics or laboratory sequence. Fuller Fresnel, thin-film, imaging and material-optics work is planned in Optics.

courses.title: Quantum I
courses.subtitle: Probability, amplitudes and wave mechanics
prerequisites: Mathematical toolkit, Classical mechanics, Electricity & magnetism and Waves. Calculus, complex numbers, ODEs, Fourier transforms, inner products and eigenvectors are used; each lesson links local preparation. Numerical shooting and spherical/radial coordinates are bridged locally.
coverage: Three dimensions and orbital angular momentum
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory single-particle nonrelativistic wave-mechanics course, not all quantum physics or a full university/laboratory credential.

courses.title: Quantum II
courses.subtitle: States, operators and composite systems
prerequisites: Quantum I and Mathematical toolkit: complex vectors, matrix products/eigenvectors, inner products, probability and calculus. Every lesson links prior local preparation; trace/partial trace, spin half-angles, coherent-state series and rotating-frame terms are taught explicitly before use.
coverage: Coupling, detuning and driven two-state models
States when outcomes or partners are unobserved
General angular momentum and orbital rotations
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory abstract-state/spin/composite course, not exhaustive quantum mastery or a university/laboratory credential.

courses.title: Quantum III
courses.subtitle: Approximation, transitions and scattering
prerequisites: Quantum II and the Mathematical toolkit. Explicit local bridges cover approximation order, Airy/delta/gauge/solid angle, continuum rates, Green/Legendre functions and Kraus maps before use. Each lesson links its precise prior preparation.
coverage: A bounded introduction to open systems
Choose, test and report an approximation
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory approximation/transition/scattering course with explicitly bounded atomic and open-system examples, not all quantum methods or a university/laboratory credential.
